output.brief: Pellacott's 2026 VA-220 valves are most likely the main cause of the failure rise, and its leak-test paperwork cannot be trusted. An outside contractor found the only VA-220 leak rig disconnected and out of service since 9 January 2026, with no VA-220 test program on any other rig. 31 of 36 certificates from 2026 reuse four number sequences that also appear in November 2025 certificates. The score rose because the certificates became complete, not because testing happened. The lab found that 11% of never-installed 2026 Pellacott valves leak at the seat, against 1% of Pellacott's 2025 valves and 0% of Durrant-Hale's. Matched claim rates are about the same for new and legacy installers and for firmware 4.1 and 4.2, so installers and firmware are not the cause. Do not release the six held lots on new certificates. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Use Durrant-Hale to cover the line stoppage. Drop the installer remediation and chargebacks. Then fix SupplierPath so test records need rig logs or a witnessed test, and check other suppliers' records. The Corlin seal and the new Line 3 can't yet be separated as the cause, so ask Pellacott to explain both. Don't order a seal switch yet.
